user_report: Rebooted, loaded the core, played the same file in Weave repeatedly; reports 5 runs total since that reboot and believes the first was missed by the poller.
capture_method: automated polling of the FTP screenshot trigger at 10.10.0.30; each poll deletes cadence_probe.png, triggers a new screenshot, fetches and decodes it, and archives any completed quiet session whose 32-bit telemetry checksum has not been seen before
capture_method_validation: six consecutive probes of a static post-run screen returned byte-identical PNGs and identical decoded telemetry, so the capture path is deterministic and the five distinct checksums represent five distinct sessions
ordinal_mapping_uncertainty: the user reports five runs since the reboot and believes run 1 was missed, but five distinct self-consistent sessions were captured and no FTP dropout was logged during the capture window, which means no reboot occurred within it. Either the five captures are runs 1 through 5, or run 1 was missed and a sixth run occurred. Capture order is certain; absolute run ordinals are not, and every trend reported here is order-based and unaffected.
poller_defect: the poller exited on reaching a four-sample target while the user was still running, so the fifth session was only recovered by a manual probe; the sample cap must be removed for subsequent blocks
findings: A zero-gap run is reachable on this build: capture 4 reported zero cadence outliers and zero missed deadlines, matching entry 564 and proving the defect is intermittent rather than universal.
Starvation falls monotonically across the capture order: 1,103,135 then 1,079,350 then 1,043,165 cycles, then a clean run with no record, then 555,422 cycles.
Bytes accepted at the ordinal-six deadline rise monotonically across the same order: 312,328 then 324,224 then 335,258 then 379,200, consistent with the media source warming.

The upstream feed rate saturates at approximately 1.38 times realtime, or about 1,392,000 B/s. Captures 2, 3 and 5 all sit at 1.38 as do entries 566 and 567, while only the colder captures fall below it at 1.30 and 1.22. This is a ceiling of the delivery path, not a continuum.

Warming alone does not prevent the miss. Capture 5 had the least starvation of any gapped run at 9.26 ms and the highest byte delivery at 379,200, yet still lost the ordinal-six slot by the same 4,004,000 cycles.
The ordinal-six miss is therefore a marginal timing race against one specific deadline rather than a simple bandwidth deficit; starvation magnitude does not predict whether the slot is lost.
Every gap in this block is exactly 4,004,000 cycles, two nominal intervals. Entry 568's 6,006,000-cycle three-interval gap remains the only one of its size.
All five sessions pass every acceptance term: 15,150,646 bytes accepted, 449 pictures, 448 swaps, error_flags 0, quiet terminal, presentation complete.
Writer and DDR remain clean in every gapped capture: upstream_fifo_pending, writer_busy and writer_capacity_blocked all false.
scope_limitations: Absolute run ordinals are unconfirmed; only capture order is established.
input_starved_cycles_since_previous_swap is a cumulative count of starved cycles within the interval, not a contiguous window, so it cannot distinguish a uniformly slow feed from a burst hole.
The snapshot holds at most three deadline records per session; runs in this block missed once each so no detail was lost.
Deinterlace mode and load history are not encoded in the snapshot and rest on the user's report.
Page-cache state is not measured; the warming interpretation remains inference from the byte-delivery and starvation trends.
This is one block from one reboot; cold sampling is still n=2 across all work to date and both cold values differ substantially at 1,659,347 and 1,103,135 cycles.
delivered_fps includes the startup hold in every run and is not a steady-state rate.
